heading: 25 October 2026 — teacher schedules pass cross-tariff coherence; route value remains open
body:
25 October 2026 — teacher schedules pass cross-tariff coherence; route value remains open
The frozen two-witness diagnostic is complete. All 159 expected stored FIT teacher plans passed the unchanged physical replay, including charging/resource/SOC checks and original load/operations consistency assertions. All 79 complete pairs were retained, plus the source1-only group for bookkeeping. No plan, timestamp, small charge, tolerance or original replay code was repaired or changed; no solver, QP or model was called.
At both source tariffs, we valued both unchanged full schedules using recomputed replay load and operations under integrated system cost c+a'L+0.5L'BL. All 79 pairs had strict own-context preference: source0's schedule beat source1's schedule under source0 prices, and source1's schedule beat source0's under source1 prices. The prespecified numerical sign band was 1e-6 generator cost units. Raw own-context gaps against the one competing schedule were exactly zero, so the concern that the other observed witness already dominates its own-context label does not occur in this two-schedule catalog. This is not global teacher optimality or a full-space regret bound.
Across the 79 groups, mean/median own-source advantages were 6.5261/6.0491 generator cost units for source0 and 32.5210/37.9361 for source1. These are absolute simulated cost units, not empirical currency, bill percentages or learned-model gains. Exact Fraction values and all nine sign-bin counts are preserved. The physical/valuation process and a separate decimal-formatting view used 2.62 displayed CPU seconds and 3.01 elapsed-sum seconds; retained rounding charges and historical unknown CPU remain explicit.
The decisive limitation is that all 31 pairs with identical movement labels also showed strict full-schedule preference reversals; all 48 differing-label pairs did too. Thus binary connection targets do not encode all economically relevant schedule response. Repricing fixed charging witnesses does not isolate the value of route changes. It rules out this simple two-witness domination concern, not teacher-search noise, charging suboptimality or a weak learning contribution.
Next is a separately frozen, small fixed-topology charging qualification/diagnostic pilot: reoptimize charging for the two stored route systems under both source tariffs, using the existing Method0 helper and independent physical replay. The design direction is six differing-label groups plus two same-label controls selected by a fixed base-ID rule, not cost magnitudes; no pilot has launched. Canonical route equality, candidate/fallback separation and numerical objective/bound uncertainty must be reviewed before interpreting route preferences. The exact fixed-column 1e-6 reporting band is not a QP accuracy guarantee. No new model fit or automatic relabeling follows. The earlier warm study's failed learned-increment threshold remains unchanged.
